text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- A Benetton store opens in central Bucharest on Monday.
- The government intends to amend the existing foreign investment law to lower profit taxes and import duties.
- The Government adopted on Sunday a bank liquidation bill and a banking draft law.

- An association of businessmen in the northeastern town of Bacau launched an appeal, calling for the removal of obstacles to private capital, demanding lower profit and wage taxes, a stop to unfair competition, unconditional sale of state assets.
- The Agriculture Ministry worked out a list of 75 state farming enterprises earmarked for privatisation and liquidation.
- Representatives of U.S. private, pension and investment funds paid a visit to Romania last week to take a look at the Romanian market.
- A new company -- Sinteza SA privately-owned chemical plant -- joins the Bucharest bourse trading on Monday.
- The tenders which the State Ownership Fund has launched so far to sell off stakes of state companies have generated thin investor interest in the enterprises on offer.
- Renel RA electricity authority signed a memorandum with Belgian Tractel Engineering on a feasibility study for a water power project on the River Olt.
- The association of construction entrepreneurs supports the road tax, saying any money spent on road maintenance would eventually help motorists spend less on car repairs.
- Carbid-Fox, a listed carbide producer, fulfilled its April export plans, shipping abroad 5,500 tonnes of carbide.
